Timeline::hours_between¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

std::int64_t Timeline::hours_between(const Timeline& other) const

Count Complete Elapsed Hours¶

hours_between() returns the signed number of complete 3,600-second units from one scalar instant to another. It compares UTC epoch nanoseconds, so timezone labels and local-clock discontinuities do not alter the duration. Any incomplete hour is discarded by truncation toward zero.

Use it when the application asks how many whole elapsed hours have passed. Do not derive that answer by comparing extracted hour() fields: those fields repeat every day and can repeat or disappear at timezone transitions.

Example: Preserve More Detail Than Whole Days¶

const auto start = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z");
const auto end = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-02T02:03:04.500000000Z");

std::cout << "days=" << start.days_between(end) << '\n'
          << "hours=" << start.hours_between(end) << '\n';

Output¶

days=1
hours=26

The same interval contains one complete 24-hour unit but 26 complete hours. The remaining minutes and seconds do not produce a 27th hour.

Example: Daylight-Saving Changes Do Not Invent Elapsed Time¶

const auto before = pluss::timeline::make("2024-03-09T10:30:00Z")
                        .tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
const auto next_civil_day = before.add_days(1);

std::cout << before.hours_between(next_civil_day) << '\n';

Output¶

23

The values share the same displayed clock on consecutive dates, but the offset transition makes their absolute separation 23 hours. hours_between() reports that absolute separation.

Example: Presentation Zones May Differ¶

const auto utc = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z");
const auto same = utc.tz_convert("America/Edmonton");

std::cout << utc.hours_between(same) << '\n';

Output¶

0

Timezone conversion changes the wall-clock view, not the instant. Both operands must still be scalar and neither may be NaT; violations throw. The method is constant-time, performs overflow-safe widened subtraction, and does not allocate or mutate either operand.

See Also¶
